question.text: The Aztecs, meanwhile, used this language, whose modern variety is still widely spoken today. The words "chipotle" and "axolotl" come from this language.
question.clue: Historians learned to write in this language at schools called calmecacs ("kahl-MAY-kahks").

swap.leadin: In trying to escape from the capital of this empire, Spanish soldiers experienced La Noche Triste [la no-chay tree-stay].
swap.text: Name this empire, led by Montezuma, which was conquered by Hernan Cortes in 1521.
swap.clue: One ruler of this empire targeted its neighbor during the Flower Wars.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about the native peoples of the Americas.
question.text: Sites from this Mesoamerican civilization include La Venta and San Lorenzo, which were mysteriously abandoned. They created giant stone heads, thought to be depictions of their rulers.
question.clue: This culture created "elongated man" figurines as well as a greenstone statue of a man holding a were-jaguar ("wair-jaguar").

swap.text: This Mesoamerican culture played the ballgame in remembrance of the mythical Hero Twins, who played it to escape Xibalba ("shee-BAL-bah"). Thirteen ballcourts were built by this culture at its site of Chichen Itza on the Yucatan Peninsula.
swap.clue: Guatemala committed a genocide against this civilization, whose howler monkey gods were chronicled in the Popul Vuh.

question.leadin: Name the following historical Mesoamerican civilizations.
question.text: This people's preclassic capital was Mirador, and they were ruled by the kuhul ajaw, mystical kings who claimed to be divine. They mysteriously disappeared after their capital Tikal collapsed.
question.clue: Their hieroglypic system was the only written language in the pre-Columbian world.

swap.leadin: The general Siyaj K'ak' overthrew the king of this city in 378 CE and replaced him with a ruler from Teotihuacan.
swap.text: Name this Mayan city in modern-day Guatemala that was home to the Lost World complex. This city fought a series of wars with the rival city of Calakmul.
swap.clue: This polity's rival was called the Snake Kingdom, and this polity's namesake hiatus began after its ruler Wak Chan K'awiil was defeated by this polity's rival and Caracol.

question.text: Inscriptions in this city lead by Pakal the Great indicate it went into a star war with another in 672 CE. An overgrown jungle in Chiapas now partly covers this city where the ball game was probably played near the Temple of the Inscriptions.
question.clue: The French explorer Jean-Frederic Waldeck resided for a time at this city, where a leafy corn plant mural is located at its "foliated cross" complex.

swap.leadin: Answer the following history bonus somewhat related to soccer, your head editor's favorite sport.
swap.text: Courts for this widespread ritualistic game have been found throughout the Americas, whose modern version is called ulama. Players of this game probably used their hips, though some may have also used rackets or bats.
swap.clue: Participants in this activity attached thin stone heads resembling ax blades to heavy belts known as yokes.

question.leadin: One of this culture's many basalt works of art is called The Wrestler.
question.text: Identify this Mesoamerican civilization whose important sites included Tres Zapotes, El Azuzul, and El Manat. Its art includes jaguar-like figures, though it's best known for its 17 colossal stone heads made of basalt.
question.clue: This Mesoamerican civilization was the first to practice ritual bloodletting and play the ball game, according to artifacts found near their cities like San Lorenzo and La Venta.

swap.leadin: This ruler sent two types of food to the strange men on "floating mountains" to see if they were humans or gods.
swap.text: Name this ruler, who, like his predecessors, held the title of tlatoani or speaker of the gods.
swap.answerHtml: Montezuma II [or Moctezuma II; or Montezuma the Young; or Moteuczoma; or Motecuhzoma; or Motēuczōmah; or Motecuhzoma Xocoyotzin]
swap.clue: Shortly after this man's death, his people assassinated the rearguard of an invading force in the Night of Sorrows massacre.

question.leadin: Identify these pre-Columbian civilizations of the Americas.
question.text: This civilization founded a number of city-states in the Yucutan Peninsula, including Tikal and Chichen Itza.
question.clue: Women like Lady Six Sky could hold the title of Ajaw amongst people of this ethnicity, who constructed a city that contains the El Caracol observatory and a temple whose shadow resembles a serpent at equinoxes.

swap.text: The final section of the Florentine Codex adopts the perspective of Tenochtitlan in describing the conquest of the Aztec Empire by this Spanish conquistador.
swap.answerHtml: Hernán Cortés [or Hernán Cortés de Monroy y Pizarro Altamirano]
swap.clue: The Florentine Codex details how this man's subordinate, Pedro de Alvarado, massacred most of the people at a festival in the Templo Mayor, leading to the retaliatory murder of this man's soldiers during La Noche Triste.

question.leadin: The supposedly "Ethiopian" features of these artworks led archaeologist Jose Melgar y Serrano to hypothesize that their makers had originated in Africa.
question.text: Name these artworks that depict men wearing protective helmets, found at sites like San Lorenzo and La Venta.
question.answerHtml: colossal heads [accept synonyms for colossal like large, titanic, enormous; accept BUT DO NOT REVEAL answers like “Olmec heads”; prompt on just heads]

swap.leadin: One artifact from this civilisation was a jade mosaic mask of a "bat god"
swap.text: Identify this pre-Columbian civilisation which had its capital at Monte Alban. The first known artifact that includes this civilisation's writing is a danzante ("dahn-SAHN-tay") stone depicting a dead and bloodied man strung upside-down.
swap.clue: The golaba, bigana and coqui("KO-kee") were officials in this civilization, whose site of Lambityeco ("lam-bee-tee-ECK-oh") is home to depictions of its chief lightning god.

question.text: The two classes of elite Aztec warriors that used the macuahuitl and recruited from all social classes were named after eagles and these animals.
question.answerHtml: jaguars [or ocēlōtl; accept jaguar warriors; accept jaguar knights; prompt on cats]
question.clue: Strange stone statues with cleft heads, such as many found by Matthew Stirling, represent an art motif referred to as a "were- ."

swap.leadin: Answer the following about some North American ruins.
swap.text: This Mayan city is located in the western portion of Honduras. It was ruled by the awesomely named Xukpi Kingdom, as well as someone name 18 Rabbit.
swap.clue: An extremely long text comprised of over 2,000 glyphs is found at this site's "Hieroglyphic Stairway."

question.leadin: These two cities experienced a "Cold War," during which B'alaj Chan K'awiil established a military outpost at Dos Pilas.
question.text: Name these two cities that fought three wars in the 6th through 8th centuries in the Peten Basin. Under "Ruler A," an ajaw from one of these cities defeated the other, leading Lady Six Sky to take power.

swap.text: The Tarascans battled this eighth king of the Aztecs, who was succeeded by Moctezuma II in 1502. This fellow famously built a temple of skulls from the sacrifced victims of the Flower Wars, and took his name from a legendary water monster.
swap.clue: Advised by his uncle Tlacaellel, this man dedicated the Templo Mayor, and gained infamy for his massive displays of human sacrifice.

question.text: The Sun Dagger glyph at this 'observatory' in New Mexico marked the position of the Sun during solstices and equinoxes. This 'observatory' containing the Fajada Butte was an important ritual site for the Pueblo people who lived in "great houses" at this 'observatory'.
question.clue: Near this site, Anna Sofaer documented a spiral petroglyph called the Sun Dagger that may track an 18.6-year lunar cycle.

swap.leadin: Even though all those damn Mesoamerican civilizations are pretty much the same, try to keep track of the one this bonus is asking about. FTPE.
swap.text: Cosijo was the rain god of this civilization, which built cities at Mitla and Yagul and counted Cosijoeza among its kings.
swap.clue: The chief god of this culture was the thunder god Cocijo.
